subject: Midquarter stitchpoint: scope rightsize & dependency asks
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Midquarter stitchpoint: scope rightsize & dependency asks

Team —

We're ~40% through Q4 and I want to run a short stitchpoint on a couple of OKRs where the runway is tight. I pulled a lightweight scope matrix (attached) and highlighted three candidate rightsizes where we can preserve impact but reduce cross-team risk. High level: 

- Proposal A: Delay non-blocking UX polish on the streaming SDK (OKR: latency/engage) and reallocate 0.4 FE FTE toward the cache-priming work.
- Proposal B: Narrow the Redwood Optimize beta to two customers (Cinder + internal infra test) instead of five to reduce integration QA time.
- Proposal C: Shift the dedicated autoscale rule work to FY27 Q1 and surface a conservative fallback policy now.

Asks: please review the attached midq_scope_matrix.xlsx and reply with: 1) which proposal you can support as-is, 2) any blocking dependencies you own (Jira links helpful), and 3) whether you can commit to a canary/rollback window if we ship the trimmed scope.

Timing: I'd like final alignment by EOD Nov 12 so the QBR deck reflects the updated plan. I'm also sharing a draft QBR_deck_v3.pdf for context (slide 6 shows the re-scope options).

Attachments: midq_scope_matrix.xlsx, QBR_deck_v3.pdf

Thanks —
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midquarter stitchpoint: scope rightsize & dependency asks

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> We're ~40% through Q4 and I want to run a short stitchpoint on a couple of OKRs where the runway is tight. I pulled a lightweight scope matrix (attached) and highlighted three candidate rightsizes...

Agree with the approach. Quick replies from my side:

- I can support Proposal B (narrow Optimize beta) fully — reduces QA hazard and still lets us capture representative telemetry. Recommend we keep one additional dev on-call for the two pilot customers for the first 10 business days.
- Proposal A: I prefer trimming the FE polish but the PM owning streaming SDK (Sofia) has a customer ask on telemetry that might require a minimal fix. If we do A, we need a 2-week carve-out for that telemetry bug.
- Proposal C: Acceptable to defer to Q1 if we accept a temporary 15% increase in cost variance risk; need an owner to manage monitoring alerts.

Dependencies I own: will assign an incident reviewer and a quick runbook for the fallback policy by Nov 8 (Jira SUP-4629).

Laura
VP, Product

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 11:04 AM Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:
> Agree with the approach. Quick replies from my side:...

Two infra notes:
1) For Proposal B (narrow Optimize beta) we can support the reduced cohort but need 48 GPU-hours for e2e load testing (SUP-4572). I've attached an infra_slot_request.csv with requested windows. Please confirm priority so I can book the pool.
2) If we shift autoscale work to Q1 (Proposal C), we should enable the conservative fallback policy this week and I can ship the monitoring for it by Nov 10. That will buy safety without the full autoscale change.

Also — if we do Proposal A and move FE headcount, please formally approve the temporary reassign in People Ops so we don't hit payroll band mismatch.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midquarter stitchpoint: scope rightsize & dependency asks

Thanks, team.

Short decision: I authorize a conservative, time-boxed rightsizing today: Approve Proposal B (narrow Optimize beta) and Proposal A (delay non-blocking FE polish) with the following conditions:

- C1: Karthik to confirm infra windows for load tests (SUP-4572) no later than Nov 6 — if not, we revert to original beta size.
- C2: Laura to publish the fallback runbook Nov 8 and assign incident reviewer.
- C3: Vanessa to own updates to customer comms for Cinder and ensure the procurement team has the QBR-ready pricing note.

Vanessa — please confirm you can sync with Cinder (Beth) and Acme procurement this week; loop procurement@acme.com for any contractual clarifications.

Markus
Chief Revenue Officer

Folks — thanks for the quick alignment. Final notes and next steps for QBR prep: 

- Karthik: I see your infra slot request; confirmed windows (Nov 9–11) and you've booked the pool. Please attach the final test report to SUP-4572 by EOD Nov 13.
- Laura: fallback runbook received and validated.
- Vanessa: please confirm customer outreach to Beth at Cinder and copy procurement@acme.com for pricing note — also add one slide in QBR_deck_v3.pdf (slide 7) about the tightened beta and customer gating.

I updated the QBR_deck_v3.pdf (link below) with the rightsized plan and impact numbers; we'll present the locked plan in the leadership readout on Nov 16. Beth — thanks for staying flexible; I've copied you for visibility.
